title: On‑prem customer requests FP8 quant profile exception and bespoke calibration with fallback validation
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Customer (Acme Health) on a Private deployment reported significant accuracy regressions after applying our default FP8 quantization profile. They requested an exception to allow a bespoke calibration run and an explicit validation pass that compares FP8, INT8 fallback, and FP16 baselines before enabling the profile in their environment.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy model with runtime-1.23 using default FP8 quant profile on a dedicated on-prem node pool
Run canonical evaluation suite (medqa-5k + diagnosis-2k prompts) with production tokenization and temperature settings
Compare metrics (NDCG@5, Exact Match, Rouge-L) against FP16 baseline collected prior to quantization
Observe 6-8% drop in NDCG and increased hallucination rate on triage prompts
observations: Regression concentrated on long-context diagnosis prompts (>1024 tokens)
Per-channel scale outliers for specific linear layers; outlier clipping at default thresholds removes high-value activations
INT8 fallback reduces regression but still shows ~1.8% NDCG gap vs FP16 for a subset of templates
Telemetry shows KV cache eviction/churn around calibration boundaries — may affect distributed cache behavior during bespoke runs
proposed_solution: Run customer-specific bespoke calibration with expanded calibration corpus (5k labeled medical QA + 2k synthetic edge-case prompts)
Test two quant strategies in parallel: FP8 with per-channel symmetric scaling + percentile-based outlier handling, and INT8 with per-tensor asymmetric scaling
Introduce a temporary quant profile exception for the customer allowing usage of the bespoke profile in their on‑prem runtime only
Implement automated validation job that computes NDCG/EM/Rouge-L and confusion matrices against holdout and returns a pass/fail based on <=1.5% NDCG drop relative to FP16
If FP8 cannot meet accuracy threshold, enable automatic routing policy to INT8 fallback for the affected model/version in the customer's environment
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Triaged with SRE and Applied ML — agreed bespoke calibration required before granting exception (Evelyn)
2026-03-04: Product approved temporary exception scoped to single model+version on customer's private deployment (PM: Jordan Blake)
2026-03-05: Security reviewed on data handling and determined no extra controls required beyond existing Private deployment KMS/audit (Sec: Maya Singh)
2026-03-07: Agreed acceptance criteria <=1.5% NDCG drop; tests must include long-context buckets and hallucination detection (Lead ML: Priya Rao)
work_done: Provisioned bespoke calibration job template in CI: confluent job quant-calib/onsite-serial-2026.03
Populated calibration corpus from customer-provided anonymized logs and internal augmentation (location: drive.redwood/Acme/med-calib-2026-03)
Ran initial FP8 calibration pass with percentile clipping 99.995 — observed persistent failure on prompt templates A3 and B7
Iterated with per-channel bias correction and dynamic clipping; INT8 path tested in parallel — INT8 showed consistent improvement on A3 but slightly worse on B7
Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2146 (calibration runner enhancements + validation reporting)
acceptance_criteria: Bespoke calibration run completes successfully on customer environment without runtime errors
Validation job shows <=1.5% relative NDCG degradation across full evaluation and <=1.0% on short-context bucket
If FP8 passes, deploy bespoke FP8 profile to customer's on‑prem runtime with rollout flags and monitoring
If FP8 fails, validate INT8 fallback meets acceptance and configure automatic routing to INT8 for that model/version
Document calibration artifacts, exact profile parameters, and a rollback plan in Confluence
